headline: The world logs a record run of days above 2C of warming, Taiwan votes under Chinese pressure, oil heads into Sunday's OPEC+ meeting near $95, and Ghana makes its first early buyback of restructured domestic bonds.

items.title: Taiwan votes in local elections as Chinese warplanes circle
items.summary: Taiwanese voters chose mayors, councillors and other officials in all 22 cities and counties on Saturday, with Taipei's race between the KMT's Chiang Wan-an and the DPP's Puma Shen in the spotlight. Taiwan accused Beijing of interference after about 33 Chinese warplane sorties; Beijing rejects the accusation and says reunification cannot be stopped.

items.title: Hamas leader's son survives Israeli strike in Gaza City
items.summary: An overnight strike hit a flat in Gaza City's Rimal area; the 29-year-old son of Hamas political chief Khalil al-Hayya survived and several relatives were hurt. Hamas called it an assassination attempt, while Israel's military said it was looking into the incident. Gaza's civil defence said seven people were killed across the territory that day.
items.source: AFP via Arab News; Al Jazeera

items.title: Italy says the drone that killed two Italians in Kuwait was Iranian-made
items.summary: Italy's foreign minister said Kuwaiti investigators found the drone was made in Iran, while noting Iran's regional allies also use such drones. Iran denies launching it, called the attack suspicious and offered to join a joint inquiry.
items.why: Gulf insecurity keeps oil, freight and fuel costs high for importers like Ghana.

items.title: Hackers breach US Air Force's Cloud One platform
items.summary: Reuters reported that unidentified hackers broke into the Air Force's main cloud platform, which hosts personnel, logistics and some military command systems. It is not yet known whether data was stolen; the Air Force declined to comment on specific networks.
items.why: A reminder that cloud and sensor data systems, including MRV platforms, need strong security.
items.videoQuery: US Air Force Cloud One hack

items.title: World logs first-ever run of days above 2C of warming
items.summary: Copernicus data show global daily temperatures stayed more than 2C above pre-industrial levels for several days in a row in late November, a first, with a new daily record on 23 November. Scientists blame long-term warming plus a strong El Niño and stress this is not yet a breach of the Paris limit, which refers to long-term averages.
items.why: Hotter years raise heat stress for fish processors working near ovens and fires.

items.title: EU and UK seal deal to link carbon markets from 2028
items.summary: The EU and UK agreed that allowances from either emissions trading system will count in both from 1 January 2028, subject to ratification, and the UK will extend its system to aviation and shipping. Both say the link could pave the way to exempting each other from their carbon border taxes; chemicals firm Ineos opposes it, saying UK carbon costs would rise.
items.why: Bigger, linked compliance markets shape future demand and prices for carbon credits.

items.title: EU sets timetable for buying CBAM certificates
items.summary: The European Commission said sales of carbon border certificates open on 1 February 2027, and importers must buy and surrender certificates for 2026 imports by 30 September 2027. One certificate covers one tonne of CO2-equivalent.
items.why: African exporters of steel, aluminium and fertiliser to Europe will start paying for embedded carbon.

items.title: Ghana pays GH¢12.9bn to buy back part of its restructured bonds early
items.summary: The government paid bondholders in cash ahead of the February 2027 maturity, retiring 44.1% of that bond under its first Domestic Debt Exchange Programme buyback. The Finance Minister announced it while closing the 2027 Budget debate in Parliament.
items.source: Government of Ghana via APO; GNA
items.why: Signals improving public finances, which affects interest rates and access to local finance.
items.videoQuery: Ghana DDEP bond buyback Ato Forson

items.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 cases
items.summary: Official data show 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths across eight provinces since the outbreak was declared in May. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine, and fighting in the east has forced some responders, including WHO staff, to evacuate.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau's military rulers postpone elections to 2028
items.summary: The transitional president issued a decree delaying the presidential and legislative votes planned for 6 December 2026 by two years, citing a lack of technical and financial means. ECOWAS had called for a quick return to civilian rule.

items.title: Fire destroys female hostel rooms at Navrongo college
items.summary: A Friday fire gutted six rooms of a female hostel at St. John Bosco's College of Education, destroying students' belongings; no one was hurt. The fire service put it out and the college arranged temporary housing while the cause is investigated.
items.videoQuery: St John Bosco College Navrongo fire

items.title: Oil heads into Sunday's OPEC+ meeting near $95
items.summary: Brent settled at $95.44 on Friday, up about 3% on the week, after tanker attacks near Hormuz, a Houthi strike on a Saudi refinery and Ukrainian drone hits on Russian refineries. Sources told Reuters OPEC+ is expected to keep early-2027 output targets unchanged at its 29 November meeting.
items.why: Oil prices feed directly into fuel, transport and LPG costs in Ghana.

items.title: Wall Street rallies in short Black Friday session
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% and the Nasdaq 2.3% as chip and AI stocks rebounded, with a chip index up nearly 5%. US online Black Friday spending was on course for a record above $13bn, according to Adobe.

items.title: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
items.summary: Nvidia told partners to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new US licence rules aimed at stopping chips reaching China. It is unclear if the pause is temporary; Nvidia did not comment.

items.title: Measles deaths hit a historic low, but vaccine gaps grow
items.summary: WHO estimates about 72,000 measles deaths in 2025, 91% fewer than in 2000, and says vaccination has saved over 60 million lives since then. Coverage has stalled at 84% for the first dose, and the US, Mexico and Bolivia lost their measles-elimination status this month.

items.title: Gavi set to restore malaria vaccine funding with $214m grant
items.summary: A grant of up to $214m via GiveWell would let Gavi return to subsidising malaria vaccines for 85% of eligible children, if its board approves in December. The vaccine is now routine in 25 African countries.
items.why: Ghana was among the first countries to roll out malaria vaccines.

good.title: Eritrea eliminates trachoma
good.summary: WHO confirmed Eritrea has ended trachoma, the top infectious cause of blindness, as a public health problem, making it the 34th country worldwide to do so. Globally, the number of people needing trachoma treatment has fallen by about 94% since 2002.

good.title: Biochar plant opens in Ghana's Ashanti Region
good.summary: Nordic Carbon says it has started turning sawmill waste, usually burned in open pits, into biochar at Drobonso, aiming for 10,000 tonnes a year and about 25,000 carbon removal credits. The company plans to supply the biochar to local farmers.
good.why: A local example of residue-to-carbon-credit business, close to Carbon Clarity's field.

good.title: Vaccine manufacturing boost for Senegal
good.summary: Gavi announced its first African Vaccine Manufacturing Accelerator payment of up to $30m to Institut Pasteur de Dakar for yellow fever vaccine work.

good.title: 'Forever chemicals' falling in English rivers
good.summary: An Environment Agency report found PFOS and PFOA levels in English waterways dropped by about 30% between 2016 and 2025 after use was restricted, and PFOS in fish nearly halved.

good.title: Wild oysters breed in Scotland's Dornoch Firth again
good.summary: Native oysters are breeding in the estuary for the first time in over a century after a restoration project released more than 140,000 since 2017.

quiz.q: From what date are the EU and UK carbon markets set to be linked?
quiz.why: Allowances from either system will count in both from 1 January 2028, subject to ratification.

quiz.q: What share of the February 2027 restructured bond did Ghana retire in its first DDEP buyback?
quiz.why: Ghana paid about GH¢12.9bn in cash to retire 44.1% of that bond early.

quiz.q: By how much have global measles deaths fallen since 2000, according to WHO?
quiz.why: WHO estimates about 72,000 deaths in 2025, 91% fewer than in 2000.

future.title: Clean cooking financed by carbon credits
future.why: New government policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in new clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits as the main engine. The catch: it only lasts if buyers trust the credits.
future.fit: This is Carbon Clarity's core. The winners will be projects with measured, audit-ready data.
future.step: This month: map which Gold Standard metered-method requirements your pilot data already meets.

future.title: Digital MRV and high-integrity credit data
future.why: Credit buyers increasingly pay only for credits they can verify. Sensor-based monitoring and clean data trails are becoming the difference between credits that sell and credits that don't.
future.fit: Your Data Vault idea could become a service for other cookstove and agriculture projects in Ghana.
future.step: Write a one-page description of the Data Vault as a service: who pays, what it proves.

future.title: Clean heat for small industries
future.why: RMI lists clean industrial heat among Africa's six emerging climate-tech opportunities. Fish smoking is exactly this: small-scale process heat.
future.fit: Improved ovens for fish processors are a clean-heat business with income for women, not just a stove programme.
future.step: Estimate the market: how many processors in Greater Accra and coastal Ghana, and how much wood they burn.

future.title: Carbon removal from biomass: biochar
future.why: RMI also highlights carbon dioxide removal that uses Africa's biomass and soils, a market where removal credits sell for far more than avoidance credits.
future.fit: Waste biomass from smoking (husks, offcuts) could be turned into biochar: a second revenue stream.
future.step: Read one biochar removal methodology and list what you'd need to measure.

future.title: Energy-led climate tech is where African investment goes
future.why: Africa's climate-tech startups raised $6.35bn from 2016 to 2025, now the continent's biggest venture sector, with energy taking about 65% of the money.
future.fit: Pitch Carbon Clarity as energy plus livelihoods: efficient heat, solar drying or cold storage for fish.
future.step: Add one slide to your pitch: 'Why energy investors should care about fish smoking'.

future.title: Article 6 advisory for Ghanaian projects
future.why: Ghana is one of the first countries trading credits between governments under Article 6. Developers need people who understand authorisation, corresponding adjustments and the Carbon Market Office process.
future.fit: Your Ghana carbon market research makes you one of those people: it can become consulting work or a job.
future.step: Turn your Step 3 agreement table into a two-page brief you can share on LinkedIn.

future.title: Solar for productive use in Africa
future.why: The IEA's World Energy Outlook 2026 projects Africa's solar capacity rising about sixfold to 234 GW by 2035 and electricity demand up 50%, yet the continent still gets only about 3% of global energy investment.
future.fit: Solar-powered fish drying, cold storage or sensor power for processors could sit alongside Carbon Clarity ovens.
future.step: Price a small solar cold-storage or dryer unit for one James Town processing group.

future.title: Benefit-sharing services for jurisdictional carbon credits
future.why: Ghana's first ART TREES credits (6.5 million tonnes, about $68m) come with a promise that communities, farmers and traditional authorities share the proceeds. Tracking who gets paid is becoming its own job.
future.fit: Your data and community skills could support transparent payment tracking for forest and cookstove programmes.
future.step: Read how Ghana's REDD+ benefit-sharing plan works and note what data it needs.
